title: Selective Prediction & Abstention
interviewAnswer: Selective prediction lets a model abstain on uncertain cases, trading coverage—the fraction answered—against risk on the answered subset.
why: High-stakes automation should sometimes know when not to decide.
intuition: Answer easy cases automatically and escalate ambiguous cases instead of forcing a low-confidence prediction.
deepDive: A reject rule thresholds a confidence/uncertainty measure; as coverage falls, accepted-case error should usually fall. The fallback path and capacity are part of the system design.
commonMistakes: Optimizing coverage without tracking accepted-case error.
Assuming the same threshold remains valid after shift.
followUps: How do you choose the abstention threshold?
production: Define fallback SLOs and monitor risk-coverage after deployment.
workedExample: OCR can accept clear forms and route ambiguous scans to manual review.
